audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings call Hero's Entrance global ('a flagged global all-in', 'a flagged global rotation'), and every spike is written without a cooldown.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140 at 4000/4750/5500 onto an ALLY. Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10 from 1150, Titan's Wrath a flat 12s, Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5, Depth Charge 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Global claim removed; the 14-second Dredge Line whiff is now the stated punish window in early, mid, wants.you[0] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings say Staggering Blow 'roots your next-hit target', which reads as if the root belongs to Galio or applies to whoever Galio hits next.
audit.why: Riot: 'Nautilus' first Attack against a target deals increased physical damage and roots THEM briefly.' It is his first auto against you that roots you — the trigger is him walking into auto range, not any action of yours.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as 'his first auto on you roots' in early, spikes[1] and whys[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings claim Depth Charge 'ignores your taunt-bait' and 'homes onto you and ignores your taunt'.
audit.why: Riot's description is a shockwave that 'CHASES an opponent', knocks up enemies it travels under, then knocks up and stuns the target. Nothing in the kit says it is unaffected by crowd control on Nautilus — the true and useful property is that once it launches you cannot walk out of it.
audit.corrected: Replaced with 'once launched it chases you and cannot be outrun' in mid, whys[6] and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells the player Dredge Line has a second use.
audit.why: Riot: 'Colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together. Colliding with TERRAIN pulls Nautilus towards it.' So a Nautilus caught in the Shield of Durand taunt radius has a wall-hook escape, and a hook aimed at terrain is not a failed engage.

edits.before: Respect the hook, not the man. At Level 1 you both have one button, but his is Dredge Line (Q) — a skillshot that drags HIM to you and lets his Staggering Blow passive root your next-hit target, so stand behind minions and never offer a clean line. Once you hit Level 3 with Winds of War, Shield of Durand and Justice Punch, the lane is yours: bait the hook, side-step, then E in, channel W and taunt-burst him in the tornado. edits.before: This is your stretch. From 4 to 6 you out-tempo him — Winds of War shoves the wave so you can E-W-Q whenever he steps up to hook, and his Titan's Wrath shield soaks one combo but not your cooldowns coming back faster than his. At 6, Hero's Entrance is the real gap: he is an immobile single-target tank, so even on a dead-even lane you can flag onto your jungler or a sidelane and win the map while his Depth Charge only locks one target. Watch his R — it's a single-target knockup that homes onto you and ignores your taunt-bait, so keep your W up to channel-tank the follow-up.

notes: Cleanest entry in the slice — no fabricated ability names — but it leaned on two claims the kit does not support. Depth Charge was described twice as ignoring the taunt; Riot's text only makes it a homing shockwave that chases the target, so I replaced the CC-immunity implication with the property that is actually true and actually useful (you cannot walk out of it once launched). And Staggering Blow was written as rooting 'your next-hit target', which inverts whose attack does the rooting: it is Nautilus's first auto against you. Added the terrain hook, which is missing from both layers and is the reason a Nautilus inside your taunt radius does not always stay there. Numbers added throughout — the 14-second Dredge Line whiff is the whole punish window and it appeared nowhere.
